fields.meta_description: Build a wedding photography questionnaire that chases quiet couples, times the family photos and turns answers into a timeline. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Wedding Photography Questionnaire That Plans the Day
fields.hero_description: Describe how you prepare for a wedding and what you need from the couple. Emergent builds the wedding photography questionnaire and keeps every couple's answers in one table.
fields.features_heading: Questions in Day Order, Answers Put to Work
fields.features_subheading: Couples answer once, weeks before the wedding. These pieces turn what they write into the plan you shoot from.
fields.feature_1:
Sections that follow the wedding day

Order the questions the way the day runs, getting ready through the last dance. Couples answer in sequence, and a gap in their timeline shows up while there is still time to fix it.
fields.feature_2:
Follow-ups that open on the answer

Ask whether the couple wants a first look. A yes opens questions on where and when; a no skips them. Flash rules at the ceremony and an unplugged ceremony branch the same way.
fields.feature_3:
A family list with names, not roles

Collect each family grouping as a row of names with how they relate to the couple. The form adds up the minutes you allow per grouping and asks for cuts once the list runs over.
fields.feature_4:
Vendor contacts on the couple's record

Gather the planner and the videographer with a phone number for each, plus the DJ or band. Every contact saves to the couple's record, ready on the day when the ceremony runs late.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders until the couple submits

Send the questionnaire with a due date. Couples who have not finished get an email reminder with a link back to where they stopped, and you get an alert if they still go quiet.
fields.feature_6:
The finished app, in your own GitHub

Export the full questionnaire app to your repository whenever you want it in-house. Every couple's answers move with it, along with the timelines and family lists built from them.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Weddings, Planned From the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
No reply in 7 days sends Maya and Jon a reminder

Wren Lake Photography sends its questionnaire to each couple well before the wedding. Maya and Jon open it, finish two of its five sections and stop. On day 7 the form emails them a reminder that links back to where they left off. When they submit, their answers fill a day-of timeline: first look at 2:30, ceremony at 4:00.
fields.tab_content_2:
Twelve groupings into 20 minutes, with two cut

Ana and Sam have a 20-minute slot for family photos. Their photographer allows 2 minutes per grouping. They list 12 groupings, which comes to 24 minutes, and the form holds the submission until they remove 2. A notes field covers family dynamics, such as divorced parents who prefer separate photos.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two getting-ready rooms, one address for each shooter

Northfield Studio sends a lead and a second photographer to most weddings. Elena gets ready at the Harbor Inn, Marcus at his brother's house. The questionnaire takes both addresses with a start time and a contact phone. Dana Cole, the lead, gets Elena's details. Luis Ortega, the second shooter, gets only Marcus's.
fields.tab_content_4:
The 13th hour goes to the photographer as a quote

Priya and Dev booked a 12-hour package for a wedding weekend. They enter 3 hours at the welcome dinner and 2 at the Sunday brunch, and the wedding day needs 8. That totals 13 hours. The form flags the extra hour and sends the photographer a note to quote it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wedding Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: The best questionnaires read like the wedding day itself. Settle which answers matter and who on your team uses each one before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write the sections in day order
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the family list by name
fields.howto_step_1_des: Lay out the questionnaire the way the day runs, with getting ready first and the reception last. Couples think through the day as they answer. A missing time stands out, because the section before it has one and the next section starts without it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for every grouping with names and relationships, such as Ana with her grandparents, Rosa and Tomas. Set how many minutes you allow per grouping. The form can then warn the couple when their list runs past the slot on the schedule.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for each getting-ready address and both venues, with a start time for every one. Add parking and vendor-entrance notes. On a team wedding, mark which photographer covers which location so nobody drives to the wrong house that morning.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent the sections, the follow-up questions and who should see which answers. The build includes the follow-up rules and a table of couples in a database you own. Change a question later by describing the change in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the date the questionnaire goes out and the date it is due. Choose when a reminder goes to the couple and when you hear about a couple who still has not answered. The chasing then happens by email without you writing each message.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give the second shooter and any assistant only the sections they need, while the lead photographer sees everything. Once the couple confirms the timeline, send the planner a copy. The venue and the photographer then work from the same times.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the first couple gets it, fill in the questionnaire as a couple would, with a family list that runs long. Check that the reminder arrives and the timeline reads right. Confirm each shooter receives only their own addresses.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is photographers' own questionnaires (Eden Strader, Honeyroot, Pancho3, a Scribd PDF), mentor posts listing what to ask (The Photographer's Mentor, Alina Thomas, Daymarked) and a Reddit thread on ranking shot priorities. Google's AI Overview lists the same sections: contacts, locations, timeline, family formals, vendors. None of them shows what happens to the answers once the couple hits submit. This page gives the questions that matter and then shows the questionnaire doing the photographer's prep: a reminder when the couple goes quiet and a timeline built from their answers, a family formal list timed against its slot, two getting-ready addresses split between lead and second shooter, and a multi-event weekend checked against the package hours.
tab_stories: Wren Lake Photography sends the questionnaire to Maya and Jon six weeks out; after 7 days without a reply the couple gets a reminder, and once they submit, their answers fill a day-of timeline with the first look at 2:30.

Priya and Dev book a 12-hour package for a three-event weekend; the form adds up 3 hours for the welcome dinner, 8 for the wedding day and 2 for the brunch, flags the 13th hour and sends the photographer a note to quote it.
